extracted.intended_audience: Navy HRM program managers, NPRDC staff, and decisionmakers evaluating MIS/HRMIN choices
extracted.subtask_description: Comparative economic and operational evaluation of the Human Resource Management Information Network (HRMIN) alternatives (in‑house vs commercial/contracting) using OMB A-76 life‑cycle and system criteria. Focus is on system performance, security, management control, maintenance, and the realized value of information to management.

rubrics_metrics.name: HRMSS stated objectives / desired outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: The HRMSS' objective is to assist in the achievement with the Navy of: improved unit readiness; improved leadership and management of human resources; improved personnel stability through retention; improved communications; improved Navy image; greater career satisfaction; demonstrated equal opportunity; increased overseas tour satisfaction and productivity; identification and reduction of drug and alcohol abuse; and increased responsiveness to both requirements and individual needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These outcomes are the high‑level goals that any HRM system (including HRMIN) should support. The text notes these objectives involve human interaction, depend on policy decisions, and assume proper staffing and resources; achieving them requires information and direction provided to decisionmakers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Purposes of management control are: (1) to assure the timely and proper implementation of program plans, (2) to maintain system inputs, processes and outputs within prescribed limits, and (3) to achieve the optimum balance between organizational effectiveness and efficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Planning and control are interdependent; control monitors performance, provides feedback, and maintains variables consistent with plans. A management information system should enable these control purposes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Information value (definition and systemic nature)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information is 'the interpretation of data to provide meaning by an individual; a tangible or intangible entity that reduces uncertainty about a state or event.' Information is systemic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An information system is a set of organized procedures that, when executed, provide information to support decision making and control. Systems should be designed to reduce uncertainty and support decision processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: MIS functional benefits (Krauss list)
rubrics_metrics.description: An MIS may help: 1) render faster decisions (detect opportunities, identify/isolate problems, define/analyze situations, evaluate alternatives); 2) accomplish more in available time (think more deeply, ponder other variables, gauge ramifications, investigate alternatives); 3) make a more thorough analysis (review more meaningful information, obtain relevant viewpoints, use advanced techniques, simulate conditions, ask 'what if' questions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The central point is time: computer processing compresses time and thereby increases decision quality/quantity. These items function as evaluative benefits when assessing whether an MIS justifies its costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management control cycle / react-and-rectify time
rubrics_metrics.description: Management control cycle stages: measurement, detection, communication, situation analysis, decisionmaking, further communication, setup/execution of corrective action — the objective is to minimize time between detection of an out-of-control condition and successful corrective action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Real-time MISs are judged by their ability to compress these time intervals. For HRM problems (time-sensitive people issues), shorter react-and-rectify time can prevent escalation and reduce costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perceived Realized Value model (Potential x Received x Utilization)
rubrics_metrics.description: Three benefit factors: Potential Contribution (P) — value attached based on specifications; Received Value (R) — portion of potential normally received by users; Utilization Value (U) — portion of received value users can actually apply. Model: Realized Value = P x R x U.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This multiplicative model measures perceived effectiveness/value of information systems; it focuses on what users actually receive and can use, not just potential capability. Use for cost‑benefit or perceived-benefit assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: System Performance and Reliability
rubrics_metrics.description: System performance was defined as how well the system supports and performs the function of the application running on it. System reliability was defined as the ability of a system to provide dependable support on a continuous basis (90% up-time and a back-up system).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Performance and reliability are primary criteria for site/operation alternatives and were ranked by the Program Manager and users. Explicit quantitative guidance: target ~90% uptime and provision of backup capability.

rubrics_metrics.name: System and Data Security
rubrics_metrics.description: Security was defined as providing an acceptable level of protection against unauthorized access to the system and to HRM Survey data.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess alternatives for their ability to protect sensitive HRM data and control system access; 'acceptable level' should be interpreted per Navy/Executive Department policies and mission sensitivity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Management Control (over system operation)
rubrics_metrics.description: The key management control factor for any alternative is the ease with which the sponsor can monitor the performance of the system and if necessary re-direct the management or content of the application so that the plans or objectives for the system are effectively used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate alternatives by the sponsor's ability to retain oversight and influence (e.g., ability to change management, reconfigure content, enforce policies). This is distinct from technical control and emphasizes administrative oversight.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintenance and Operational Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Capability of an alternative to provide ongoing maintenance and operational support for the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes software maintenance, operator staffing (e.g., RJE operator to load new data), site‑unique support costs, transition complexity, and the availability of technical expertise to manage/operate HRMIN. Considerations noted: NPRDC developed the system and has corporate knowledge, in‑house software reduces maintenance problems, conversion costs and user interruptions can be avoided by staying at NPRDC.
